sent_to_model:
My Nana is moving out of her house in Sudbury into a retirement place on the 21st and I can't be there, I'm primary on call that whole week and couldn't find anyone to swap. My aunt Denise is driving up and said she'll read Nana a letter from me the night before the move, while they're sitting in the kitchen one last time. I want to write her a proper long one, not a card. Honestly I've been putting it off because every time I start I get choked up and then I just close the laptop. Can you help me get it down? I've been dumping stuff into a note on my phone all week, pasting it below. It's ok if it makes her cry a bit but I don't want it to be all sad, she's actually kind of excited about the new place.

- move date Sat Nov 21, new place is Elmwood Terrace, 2nd floor, room looks at the parking lot and a big maple
- house on Kathleen St, she's been there 51 years, Grandpa Walt died 2019
- she's 88, still plays crib Tuesdays with the church ladies
- Denise is taking the cuckoo clock and the cedar chest, I asked for the crib board
- I'm coming up Dec 5 weekend once rotation's done
- summers at the house as a kid, she let me stay up to watch the Expos/Jays on the little TV in the kitchen if I dried dishes
- she taught me crib at like 7 and never once let me win, first time I skunked her I was 15 and she made me a whole pan of butter tarts
- when I got the job in Toronto she mailed me a $20 bill taped in a card saying "for pizza, you look thin on the computer"
- last Christmas my pager went off during dinner and she asked if the internet was broken again and if I fixed it. Now she asks every call "did anything break"
- the back steps, she'd sit there with tea at 6am, I'd come out and she'd never talk till the cup was done
- I feel guilty not being there, I know it's dumb, everyone says it's fine
- she raised half the family in that kitchen, the house is kind of her
- Elmwood actually looks nice, they have a crib league lol
- tell her I'm proud of her for doing it herself, she picked it, nobody made her
- I want her to know what the house meant to me without making it a funeral
- make her laugh at least twice
- end with something about Dec 5 and the crib board, first game at the new place

(About me: site reliability engineer, 34, Toronto, Canada. Length: it should come to roughly 800-2,000 words.)

must_cover: Explains why the writer cannot be there for the move.
Tells Nana what her house and their shared memories mean to the writer.
Expresses pride in Nana choosing the new place herself.
Closes with the December 5 visit and a first crib game with the board at her new place.
Includes at least two moments intended to make Nana laugh.
